overall_summary: Bitcoin is trying to stabilize after heavy long liquidations, but the broader tape stays risk-off. Persistent ETF outflows, rising yields, a stronger dollar, and hawkish inflation data are weighing on sentiment, while escalating Middle East and shipping tensions add another layer of caution. Extreme fear and dip-buying hints offer some contrarian support, yet the near-term bias remains defensive until macro and geo risks ease.
key_points: ETF outflows stretch to a seventh day
Yields and dollar strength pressure risk assets
Hawkish PPI keeps Fed tightening bets alive
Middle East tanker and base attacks elevate risk
Extreme fear plus Saylor dip-buy hints cushion

items.title: Bitcoin Rebounds to $64K After $62K Low, $2B Long Liquidations
items.summary: Bitcoin plunged to about sixty-two thousand dollars over the weekend, its lowest since mid-July, wiping out roughly two billion dollars in mostly long leveraged positions. It has since clawed back above sixty-four thousand. The move extends a sixth straight weekly loss and a seventeen percent November drop, with traders now watching Nvidia earnings Tuesday and Fed minutes. A big liquidation flush like this often clears weak hands, but the bounce still needs to hold key levels.
items.impact: Heightened short-term volatility around support ahead of major tech and macro catalysts

items.title: Spot Bitcoin ETFs Log Seventh Straight Day of Outflows
items.summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs saw about one hundred eighty-five million dollars leave on Friday, extending the outflow streak to seven sessions and roughly one point nine billion dollars since early November. BlackRock’s IBIT led the redemptions. November total outflows are running over two billion. Persistent institutional selling removes a key bid and keeps pressure on price until flows reverse.
items.impact: Sustained selling pressure and weaker spot demand until inflows return

items.title: Luxor Hit by AI-Enabled Attack Redirecting Miner Hashrate
items.summary: Bitcoin mining firm Luxor confirmed attackers used its Commander fleet software to redirect hashrate from more than a dozen client accounts to the OCEAN pool over the weekend. Early unverified reports put the diverted power near thirteen exahashes. Luxor patched it in two hours, restored machines, and pledged full compensation. CEO Nick Hansen called it a sophisticated AI-enabled vector and warned crypto firms face rising AI attacks. Actual stolen rewards were tiny, under a quarter Bitcoin.
items.impact: Operational risk spotlight for mining infrastructure with limited direct price effect

items.title: JPMorgan and DBS Launch 24/7 Tokenized Dollar Transfers
items.summary: JPMorgan’s Kinexys and Singapore’s DBS have gone live with instant cross-border transfers of tokenized US dollar deposits between the US and Singapore, including weekends. Ant International is the first client using it for treasury management. This is bank deposits on permissioned blockchains, not crypto tokens, but it marks real institutional adoption of on-chain money movement. It supports broader tokenization efforts led by Singapore’s central bank.
items.impact: Positive signal for institutional blockchain and tokenization rails

items.title: Michael Saylor Hints Strategy May Buy the Bitcoin Dip
items.summary: Strategy executive chairman Michael Saylor posted the company’s Bitcoin purchase tracker on Sunday with the line this dip could use a little orange, his usual signal before accumulation disclosures. Strive’s CEO posted a similar buy-the-dip message. No new purchase is confirmed yet in filings, but the market reads it as intent to add while Bitcoin sits near sixty-two to sixty-five thousand. Strategy already holds over eight hundred fifty thousand Bitcoin.
items.impact: Potential large institutional bid that could support a floor if confirmed

items.title: Crypto Fear and Greed Index Hits Extreme Fear Near 10
items.summary: The Crypto Fear and Greed Index dropped to around ten, extreme fear, its lowest readings since June and matching the weekend price washout. Bitcoin is down roughly thirteen to seventeen percent on the week and month while leveraged longs got flushed. Historically extreme fear often coincides with washed-out conditions that can set up relief, but it is not a timing tool by itself. Traders are treating it as a sentiment extreme while waiting for Nvidia and macro catalysts this week.
items.impact: Signals capitulation risk is elevated; potential for relief bounce if catalysts cooperate

items.title: US 10-Year Yield Tops 5.14%, DXY Hits Multi-Month Highs
items.summary: Treasury yields climbed sharply last week and remain elevated near 5.13 to 5.15 percent on the 10-year, with the dollar index pushing to fresh highs around 103.4 to 103.5. The move stems from hotter-than-expected October CPI and PPI readings plus hawkish Fed comments that forced markets to price in more rate hikes. Crypto traders should care because higher real yields and a stronger dollar tighten financial conditions and historically pressure Bitcoin and risk assets.
items.impact: Higher yields and USD strength headwind for BTC and risk assets

items.title: Fed Chair Warsh Speaks Today Amid December Hike Bets
items.summary: Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh delivers opening remarks today at a productivity and jobs conference, with other officials including Barr and Williams also speaking. Markets have fully priced a 25 basis point hike in December and assign a smaller chance to 50 basis points after sticky inflation and recent Fed comments. Traders will parse any signal on the path of rates, which directly drives liquidity and Bitcoin volatility.
items.impact: Hawkish tone could extend yield rally and pressure crypto; dovish would ease

items.title: China October Data Misses: Retail Sales, Output Slow Sharply
items.summary: China reported retail sales up just 0.4 percent year-over-year in October, well below the 0.8 percent forecast, while industrial production slowed to 4.8 percent from 5.5 percent and fixed-asset investment contracted further to minus 8.1 percent year-to-date. Domestic demand remains soft even as exports hold up on AI-related goods. Weak Chinese data weighs on global growth expectations and commodity currencies, adding a risk-off tone that can spill into crypto.
items.impact: Softer global growth and risk appetite negative for Bitcoin

items.title: Markets Brace for Tuesday Retail Sales and Wednesday FOMC Minutes
items.summary: The key U.S. data this week is October retail sales on Tuesday, expected to slow from September’s strong 0.8 percent gain, plus industrial production. Wednesday brings the minutes from the October FOMC meeting that held rates at 3.75 to 4 percent with two dissents for a hike. These releases will test whether consumer demand can handle higher yields and clarify how many officials wanted tighter policy, setting the tone for December.
items.impact: Data surprises could reprice Fed path and move yields, dollar, and crypto

items.title: October PPI Hits 6.5% Yearly High, Reinforcing Hawkish Fed View
items.summary: Producer prices rose 0.3 percent month-over-month in October but the yearly rate climbed to 6.5 percent, the highest since late 2022, after a big September revision. Core measures also stayed firm. Combined with the earlier hot CPI print, this data locked in market expectations for additional Fed tightening and helped drive the recent yield spike that is still echoing into Monday trading.
items.impact: Sticky wholesale inflation supports higher-for-longer rates, pressuring risk assets

items.title: Empire State Survey Due Today; Fed Speakers Flag More Tightening
items.summary: The New York Fed Empire State Manufacturing Index for November prints this morning, following a strong October reading of 25.5. New York Fed President Williams recently said inflation remains far too high and more rate increases will likely be needed. Multiple Fed speakers today keep policy front and center while markets await the next hard data points.
items.impact: Soft print could ease hike fears slightly; strong data or hawkish talk extends pressure

items.title: Iran reports multiple tankers hit by mines in Strait of Hormuz
items.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say two more oil tankers struck naval mines and caught fire while trying an unauthorized southern route through the Strait of Hormuz, bringing the weekend total to around six vessels ablaze or sinking. Tehran blames U.S. guidance and warns shipowners the southern lane is mined. Traders should care because this chokepoint handles a huge share of global oil; fresh disruption risks keep energy prices volatile and feed broader risk-off pressure even if supply looks ample on paper.
items.impact: Oil volatility spike and risk-off for equities and crypto

items.title: China confirms first Xi-Trump-Putin trilateral summit in Shenzhen
items.summary: Beijing has officially confirmed that Xi Jinping will host Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin for their first-ever three-way summit on November 19 in Shenzhen on the sidelines of APEC. Talks are expected to cover nuclear arms, the Iran conflict, and strategic stability, though Ukraine may stay off the U.S. agenda. For traders this is a high-stakes event that could ease or harden major flashpoints and move risk sentiment depending on any signals of de-escalation or grand bargains.
items.impact: Potential volatility around diplomacy outcomes on nuclear and Middle East issues

items.title: Third U.S. aircraft carrier arrives in Middle East amid Iran tensions
items.summary: The USS Theodore Roosevelt has entered the CENTCOM area, joining two other U.S. carriers already operating near Iran and bringing more than 20,000 sailors and hundreds of aircraft into the theater. This rare three-carrier presence comes as Washington weighs further action and Iran continues asymmetric moves. Crypto and risk traders should watch because it signals possible renewed escalation that can tighten oil supply fears and push markets into defensive mode.
items.impact: Heightened military posture raises war-premium and risk aversion

items.title: Iran launches fresh drone attacks on U.S. base in Bahrain
items.summary: Iran's forces launched drones at a U.S. military facility in Bahrain, with Bahraini defenses claiming interceptions in the latest of several recent attempts. Gulf states have condemned the moves amid the ongoing U.S.-Iran conflict. This matters for markets because attacks on host-nation bases raise the chance of wider Gulf involvement and keep insurance and shipping costs elevated through the energy corridor.
items.impact: Escalation risk in Gulf supports oil and weighs on risk assets

items.title: Ukraine hits Crimea bridge in record 1,336-drone barrage
items.summary: Ukraine launched one of its largest drone attacks of the war, with Russia claiming 1,336 intercepts overnight; the barrage struck the Kerch Bridge linking Russia to Crimea, briefly halting traffic and causing minor reported damage. Hundreds of drones targeted the Moscow region. Ahead of the Trump-Putin-Xi meeting this keeps the Ukraine front hot and can complicate any diplomatic optics while reminding markets that the conflict remains a source of energy and commodity disruption.
items.impact: War escalation noise increases geopolitical risk premium

items.title: Houthis seize key Red Sea coast after Yemeni forces retreat
items.summary: Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces have withdrawn from positions overlooking the Bab al-Mandab Strait to reinforce Aden, leaving Iran-aligned Houthis in control of the strategic coastal area. Houthis are also advancing closer to Aden itself. Traders care because this second major chokepoint after Hormuz threatens Asia-Europe shipping lanes and LNG/oil flows, adding another layer of freight and insurance risk.
items.impact: Shipping disruption risk compounds energy and trade volatility
